title: Jailer 2 Crosses Rs 600 Crore Worldwide as India Gross Hits Rs 374 Crore
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel closed its extended first week with the biggest Kollywood India total ever, and trade trackers put its eight-day worldwide gross at about Rs 606 crore — within reach of 2.0's all-time record.
body:
• Jailer 2 closed its eight-day extended first week at about Rs 374 crore gross in India on Pinkvilla's tally — the biggest extended week ever for a Tamil film, passing 2.0's Rs 365 crore.
  • Worldwide, the Rajinikanth starrer has crossed Rs 600 crore: Sacnilk-based reporting put the eight-day worldwide gross at about Rs 606 crore, including roughly $22 million from overseas.
  • On its current trend, the film is expected to pass 2.0 this weekend to become the highest-grossing Kollywood film of all time worldwide.
  • Kerala and Karnataka have already given the film their biggest-ever Kollywood totals, and Tamil Nadu collections of about Rs 139 crore are trending ahead of Leo and The GOAT at the same stage.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has closed its extended first week at the top of Tamil cinema's record books. Pinkvilla reported that the film grossed about Rs 18.50 crore in India on Thursday, its eighth day, taking its extended-week India gross to about Rs 374 crore — the biggest ever for Kollywood, surpassing the Rs 365 crore that 2.0 collected in 2018. Overseas, Pinkvilla put the film at about $22 million, or Rs 209 crore, for a worldwide total near Rs 583 crore at the close of Thursday's India business.

Trade trackers counting the full eighth day put the film over the next milestone already. Filmfare, citing Sacnilk estimates, reported a worldwide gross of Rs 606.05 crore after eight days, with India net collections of Rs 17.15 crore on day eight — a drop of about 39% from Wednesday — across more than 13,000 shows. Estimates differ between trackers, as box office reporting in India is compiled from trade sources rather than audited figures, but both tallies agree on the direction: the film has passed Leo and the original Jailer in eight days and is closing on 2.0.

Where the money came from

Pinkvilla's territorial breakdown shows a run powered well beyond the home state. Tamil Nadu contributed about Rs 139 crore, the Andhra Pradesh–Telangana market Rs 71.25 crore, Karnataka Rs 64 crore and Kerala Rs 63 crore, with Rs 36.75 crore from the rest of India. The film is already the highest-grossing Kollywood release ever in both Kerala and Karnataka. In the Telugu states it ranks third, behind 2.0 and Jailer, and Pinkvilla expects it to overtake both and possibly become the first Tamil film to cross Rs 100 crore there.

The day-wise pattern explains both the record and Thursday's dip. The film opened at Rs 67.50 crore in India, held above Rs 48 crore through the festive stretch, and grossed Rs 52.50 crore on Tuesday before the holiday effect faded — Wednesday fell to Rs 31.50 crore and Thursday, the first largely normal working day, to Rs 18.50 crore, a 40% drop. A fall of that size after an extended holiday week is typical for an event film; the question for the second weekend is the size of the Saturday rebound.

What the run means

For the diaspora audience that drives a large share of overseas Tamil collections — the film's $22 million international gross is nearly 36% of its worldwide total — Jailer 2 extends a pattern set by Jailer in 2023, when Rajinikanth's film became a North American record-setter for Tamil cinema. The sequel, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, adds Hrithik Roshan in his Tamil cinema debut alongside returning faces including Mohanlal and Shiva Rajkumar, a casting spread designed to pull audiences across India's language markets at once.

Pinkvilla expects the film to become the highest-grossing Kollywood film of all time worldwide by Sunday, passing 2.0's lifetime total. In Tamil Nadu, its Rs 139 crore is the third-highest eight-day figure, behind Leo (Rs 173 crore) and The GOAT (Rs 142 crore), but it is trending more strongly than both at the same stage. The second weekend will decide whether this is remembered as a front-loaded festive run or the biggest Tamil grosser ever — on current numbers, it is on course to be both.
